children.name: Callipepla
children.description: Elegant quail with a distinctive forward-curving plume of feathers on the crown, composed of six upright feathers. They are adapted to arid and semi-arid landscapes of western North America.

children.name: Callipepla californica
children.description: The California quail, also known as the California valley quail or Valley quail, is a small ground-dwelling bird in the New World quail family, inhabiting western North America. It is the state bird of California.

children.name: Callipepla gambelii
children.description:
Gambel's quail (Callipepla gambelii) is a small ground-dwelling bird in the New World quail family. It inhabits the desert regions of Arizona, California, Colorado, New Mexico, Nevada, Utah, Texas, and Sonora; also New Mexico-border Chihuahua and the Colorado River region of Baja California. Gambel's quail is named in honor of William Gambel, a 19th-century naturalist and explorer of the Southwestern United States.
The species is not as widely introduced as the related California quail. It was, however, released on San Clemente Island in 1912 by Charles T. Howland et al., where it is currently still established.

children.name: Callipepla squamata
children.description: The scaled quail (Callipepla squamata), also commonly called blue quail or cottontop, is a species of the New World quail family.

children.name: Colinus
children.description: Small, plump quail with mottled brown plumage and a distinctive white or buff facial stripe. They are highly social, forming coveys that forage together on the ground.

children.name: Colinus virginianus
children.description: The northern bobwhite (Colinus virginianus), also known as the Virginia quail or (in its home range) bobwhite quail, is a ground-dwelling bird native to Canada, the United States, Mexico, and Cuba, with introduced populations elsewhere in the Caribbean, Europe, and Asia.

children.name: Colinus nigrogularis
children.description: The Yucatan bobwhite or black-throated bobwhite (Colinus nigrogularis) is a species of bird in the family Odontophoridae.

children.name: Colinus leucopogon
children.description:
The spot-bellied bobwhite (Colinus leucopogon) is a ground-dwelling bird in the New World quail family. It is sometimes considered to be conspecific with the crested bobwhite, Colinus cristatus.
The spot-bellied bobwhite is found in El Salvador, Guatemala, Honduras, Nicaragua and Costa Rica in open savanna with bushes and trees and other open woodland.

children.name: Colinus cristatus
children.description: The crested bobwhite (Colinus cristatus) is a species of bird in the family Odontophoridae.

children.name: Cyrtonyx
children.description: Distinctive, stocky quail with an extremely short tail and an intricately patterned plumage of black, white and chestnut. They are among the most beautiful but secretive of the New World quail.

children.name: Cyrtonyx montezumae
children.description: The Montezuma quail (Cyrtonyx montezumae) is a stubby, secretive New World quail of Mexico and some nearby parts of the United States.

children.name: Cyrtonyx ocellatus
children.description: The ocellated quail is a species of bird in the family Odontophoridae, the New World quail. It is found in El Salvador, Guatemala, Honduras, Mexico, and Nicaragua.

children.name: Dactylortyx
children.description: A monotypic genus of quail with a beautiful song.

children.name: Dactylortyx thoracicus
children.description: The singing quail (Dactylortyx thoracicus) is a species of bird in the family Odontophoridae, the New World quail.

children.name: Dendrortyx
children.description: Dendrortyx — a genus of new world quail in the family Odontophoridae.

children.name: Dendrortyx barbatus
children.description: The bearded wood partridge is a bird species in the family Odontophoridae, the New World quail. It inhabits the Sierra Madre Oriental of Mexico.

children.name: Dendrortyx leucophrys
children.description: The buffy-crowned wood partridge is a bird species in the family Odontophoridae, the New World quail. It is found in Mexico, Guatemala, Honduras, El Salvador, Costa Rica and Nicaragua.

children.name: Dendrortyx macroura
children.description: The long-tailed wood partridge is a bird species in the family Odontophoridae, the New World quail. It is found only in Mexico.

children.name: Nanortyx
children.description: Nanortyx — a genus of new world quail in the family Odontophoridae.

children.name: Odontophorus
children.description: Stocky forest quail found in Central and South America.

children.name: Odontophorus atrifrons
children.description: The black-fronted wood quail (Odontophorus atrifrons) is a bird species in the family Odontophoridae, the New World quail. It is found in Colombia and Venezuela.

children.name: Odontophorus balliviani
children.description: The stripe-faced wood quail (Odontophorus balliviani) is a species of New World quail. It is found in Bolivia and Peru.

children.name: Odontophorus capueira
children.description:
The spot-winged wood quail (Odontophorus capueira) is a species of bird in the family Odontophoridae. It is found in Brazil, Argentina and Paraguay, and formerly in Uruguay. In Portuguese and Spanish the bird is called uru.
Its natural habitats are subtropical or tropical dry lowland forests. Its population is thought to be declining but at a moderate rate, so the International Union for Conservation of Nature has assessed it as being a "least-concern species".

children.name: Odontophorus columbianus
children.description: The Venezuelan wood quail (Odontophorus columbianus) is a bird species in the family Odontophoridae, the New World quail. It is found in the Venezuelan Coastal Range.

children.name: Odontophorus dialeucos
children.description: The Tacarcuna wood quail (Odontophorus dialeucos) is a species of bird in the family Odontophoridae, the New World quail. It is found in Colombia and Panama.

children.name: Odontophorus erythrops
children.description: The rufous-fronted wood quail (Odontophorus erythrops) is a species of bird in the family Odontophoridae, the New World quail. It is found in Colombia and Ecuador.

children.name: Odontophorus guianensis
children.description: A wood quail from the Guiana Shield.

children.name: Odontophorus guttatus
children.description:
The spotted wood quail (Odontophorus guttatus) is a small ground-dwelling bird in the New World quail family. It is a resident breeder in the mountains of Central America from southern Mexico to western Panama.
It occurs in highlands from 1000 m or higher up to the timberline, usually in dense understory thickets or bamboos. The nest, as with several other wood-quails remains undescribed, but the eggs are known to be creamy-white with brown spots.

children.name: Odontophorus hyperythrus
children.description: The chestnut wood quail (Odontophorus hyperythrus) is a bird species in the family Odontophoridae, the New World quail. It is found only in Colombia.

children.name: Odontophorus leucolaemus
children.description: The black-breasted wood quail (Odontophorus leucolaemus) is a bird species in the family Odontophoridae. It is found in Costa Rica and Panama. Its natural habitat is subtropical or tropical moist montane forest.

children.name: Odontophorus melanonotus
children.description: The dark-backed wood quail (Odontophorus melanonotus) is a bird species in the family Odontophoridae, which is the New World quail. It is found in Colombia and Ecuador.

children.name: Odontophorus melanotis
children.description:
The black-eared wood quail (Odontophorus melanotis) is a bird species in the order Galliformes. Until recently, the species was thought to be part of the family Phasianidae (Old World quail) however DNA-DNA hybridization results determined that black-eared wood quail are only distantly related to Old World quail. As a result, black-eared wood quail have been placed in the family Odontophoridae (New World quail) and more specifically, in the category of wood quail (genus Odontophorus).
There is limited information available on this species, but black-eared wood quail are considered to be forest-adapted, monogamous, relatively large pheasant-like birds that can be found in tropical and subtropical forests of Central America. They feed on insects and fruit and can be solo or in small groups.

children.name: Odontophorus speciosus
children.description: The rufous-breasted wood quail is a species of bird in the family Odontophoridae. It is found in Bolivia, Ecuador, and Peru primarily on the east side of the Andes between 800 and 2000m in elevation.

children.name: Odontophorus stellatus
children.description: The starred wood quail (Odontophorus stellatus) is a species of bird in the family Odontophoridae (New World quail). It is found in subtropical or tropical moist lowland forests of Bolivia, Brazil, Ecuador, and Peru.

children.name: Odontophorus striolatus
children.description: A wood quail from the western Amazon.

children.name: Oreortyx
children.description: A monotypic genus of the largest New World quail, characterised by a long, straight black plume rising vertically from the crown. It is an expert runner and prefers rugged, mountainous terrain.

children.name: Oreortyx pictus
children.description: The mountain quail (Oreortyx pictus) is a small ground-dwelling bird in the New World quail family.

children.name: Philortyx
children.description: A monotypic genus of quail from western Mexico.

children.name: Philortyx fasciatus
children.description: The banded quail (Philortyx fasciatus) is a species of bird in the family Odontophoridae.

children.name: Ptilopachus
children.description: Ptilopachus — a genus of new world quail in the family Odontophoridae.

children.name: Ptilopachus petrosus
children.description: The stone partridge is a bird of the New World quail family. This largely brown bird, which commonly holds its tail raised, is found in scrubland and lightly wooded habitats, often near rocks, from Kenya and Ethiopia to Gambia.

children.name: Rhynchortyx
children.description: A monotypic genus of quail from Central and South America.

children.name: Rhynchortyx cinctus
children.description: The tawny-faced quail (Rhynchortyx cinctus) is a species of bird in the family Odontophoridae, the New World quail. It is found in Colombia, Costa Rica, Ecuador, Honduras, Nicaragua, and Panama.
